newsitem.title: USA: Judge blocks Calif. welfare cuts to new residents.
newsitem.headline: Judge blocks Calif. welfare cuts to new residents.

text.p: A federal judge has issued an order that will prevent California from cutting welfare benefits to needy families new to the state, attorneys said on Monday.

Attorneys for the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and the state said U.S. District Judge David Levi issued a preliminary injunction blocking California from enacting the welfare reductions until the case goes to trial .
California Gov. Pete Wilson, a Republican, said the state would appeal the decision. The order was issued late Friday, according to the attorneys.
State lawmakers planned to reduce benefits to welfare recipients who have not lived in California for 12 consecutive months to the levels they received in the states they left.
The ACLU sued the state earlier this year to block the cuts, alleging that the reductions in welfare grants would violate the U.S. Constitution.
Wilson argued that the reductions were needed because "California's generous grant makes us a welfare magnet state."
